instruction: Can you help me switch back to the old Chrome UI by disabling the two 2023 refresh features?

metadata.explanation: This is another paraphrased variation of the original task. The instruction uses different wording ('latest Chrome interface isn't working well' vs 'do not like the design', 'help me revert to the old Chrome UI' vs 'keep using the original one', 'disabling both the 2023 refresh experiments' vs 'disable the new 2023 version chrome UI') but the core task remains the same: disable the chrome-refresh-2023 and chrome-webui-refresh-2023 experiments. The config and evaluator are identical.

llm_judge_reasons: Evaluator logic is semantically correct and properly verifies the instruction requirements
Getter 'get_enabled_experiments' correctly extracts list of currently ENABLED experiments from Chrome's Local State file (chrome.py:319-351)
Expected value is correctly set to empty list: rules.names = []
Logic flow verification: When experiments are successfully DISABLED → get_enabled_experiments returns [] → metric checks [] == [] → returns 1.0 (PASS)
Logic flow verification: When experiments remain ENABLED → get_enabled_experiments returns ['chrome-refresh-2023@1', ...] → metric checks ['chrome-refresh-2023', ...] == [] → returns 0.0 (FAIL)
Postconfig appropriately restarts Chrome (pkill + relaunch) to ensure settings are loaded fresh for verification
The evaluator will correctly pass when task is completed (experiments disabled) and fail when task is incomplete (experiments still enabled)
